title: A Coupled Experiment-finite Element Modeling Methodology for Assessing High Strain Rate Mechanical Response of Soft Biomaterials
protocol: Wear personal protective equipment in accordance with standard biosafety protocols of the laboratory and/or institution.
Obtain porcine tissue (head, abdomen, or hind leg) of healthy pigs from a local abattoir within 1-2 hr post mortem.
Store porcine tissue in biohazard safety bags and then place them in an iced container (~5.56-7.22 °C).
Transport porcine tissue to the nearest laboratory for dissection.
Under supervision, surgically extract porcine organ (brain, liver, muscle, fat, or tendon) and place them in containers filled with phosphate buffered saline (PBS) for temporary storage (pH 7.4).
Store PBS containers in an iced cooler (~5.56-7.22 °C) and immediately transport them to the testing facility.
Remove porcine organ from the PBS container.
Place the porcine organ on a sterile surface.
Identify the primary fiber orientation and locations for each test sample.
Use a cylindrical die with a 30 mm inner diameter to dissect the test sample from the porcine organ.
Inject PBS through the opposite end of the dissection tool if the test sample is wedged inside the die.
Place the extracted test sample on a separate area of the sterile surface.
Trim the sample to the prescribed thickness and aspect ratio using a scalpel.
Measure the thickness and diameter at three different locations with calipers.
Store all test samples in fresh PBS until SHPB device readiness.
Ensure that samples are tested within 4 hr after slaughter.
Discard non-cylindrical samples due to incision errors or variations in cross-section.
Place discarded samples in biohazard safety bags.
Repeat steps for obtaining additional test samples if needed.
Place the striker bar, incident bar, and transmitted bar in metal stanchions for SHPB testing.
Ensure that bars are free moving and their interfaces are aligned with each other.
Provide a stopper for the transmitted bar for safety.
Connect the strain gages adhered to incident and transmitted bars to the signal amplifier.
Turn on the signal conditioning amplifiers and the DAQ module computer.
Initialize the high speed data capturing software.
Verify the live capturing of the signals to see if they lie within the normal range.
Nullify the noise signals by clicking the zero icon.
Input the trigger level and the data rate (2 MHz).
Initialize the software to record once the trigger level has been achieved.
Load the striker bar adjacent to the pressure chamber.
Fill the pressure chamber to a desired pressure.
Zero out the laser speed meter by pressing the zero button.
Set the reflector strip on the striker bar behind the laser sensors.
Place the sample confinement chamber such that it does not hinder the movement of incident and reflected bar.
Place the incident bar in contact with the transmitted bar.
Run a test (without a sample) by turning on trigger switch for the pressure chamber on the striker bar.
Once the data is acquired in the computer, save and analyze the SHPB strain gage data to ensure that the testing procedure is functioning properly.
Place the cylindrical sample between the incident and transmitted bar.
Close the sample confinement chamber.
Perform Tasks 3.4-3.7 with the sample placed between the incident and transmitted bars.
Ensure that the sample centerline aligns with the bar centerline.
Check that the sample is not compressed and maintains its previous geometry.
Remove sample debris from the incident bar using disposable sanitary wipes.
Dispose of sample debris in biohazard safety bags.
Clean the incident bar, transmitted bar, and sample confinement chamber with 70% ethanol solution.
Sanitize the bars and sample confinement chamber after cleaning.
Open the “MSU High Rate Software” for analysis of Hopkinson Bar waves.
Select the “Tension/Compression” option in the Mode Tab for uniaxial testing.
Choose “2 Gages” in the Gages Tab and click “Continue.”
Navigate to the incident wave data from the strain gage record on the incident bar.
Import the transmitted bar strain gage record.
Input physical parameters of the test setup including bar dimensions, voltage to strain factors, strain gage positions, and viscoelastic dispersion constants.
Select the Data Tab in the Main Window.
Use cursor bars to reduce the dataset to only the amount containing incident, reflected, and transmitted waves.
Click “Continue.”
Select the Select Waves Tab in the Main Window.
Confine the incident wave in the Incident Wave Graph using cursor bars.
Confine the reflected wave in the Reflected Wave Graph using cursor bars.
Confine the transmitted wave in the Transmitted Wave Graph using cursor bars.
Click “Continue.”
Select the Correct Tab in the Main Window to correct for viscoelastic dispersion.
Select the Shift Tab in the Main Window.
Drag the incident, reflected, and transmitted waves to the same initial position in time in the Wave Graph.
View all of the waves in the Data Graph.
Once completed, click “Continue.”
In the results file, save load, displacement, position, and velocity profiles by clicking “Save As.”
Calculate true stress and true strain using specimen dimensions measured before the Hopkinson Bar test with Microsoft Excel or any other spreadsheet software.
Using commercial finite element (FE) software, create a FE model of the SHPB setup.
Assign an initial velocity to the FE model of the striker bar to initialize the FE simulation.
Create a FE model of the SHPB setup without a sample.
Run the FE simulation.
Assign material properties for polymeric bars as given in Table 1.
Verify agreement between strain gage measurements from experiment and FE simulation.
Incorporate biomaterial sample into the FE model of the SHPB setup.
Implement ISV material model to the biomaterial sample in vumat file format.
Perform a mesh refinement study using three different mesh sizes.
Analyze results to determine solution convergence.
Select the FE model with the lowest mesh size that converges after further simulations.
Conduct the two-step FE model calibration.
Upload experimental data into the one-dimensional implement of the ISV material model.
Calibrate true stress-stain curve of the experiment with the model’s true stress-strain curve by adjusting parameters.
Assign ISV material constants to the biomaterial sample in the FE model of the SHPB setup.
Run the FE simulation with striker bar velocity and sample deformation strain rate corresponding to the SHPB tests at the same strain rate.
Compare the strain gage measurements from experiment and FE simulation for good agreement (strain versus time).
Perform a volume average of the loading direction (Σ33) stress along the centerline elements of the FE model sample.
